title: The plus construction is separated and injects into its double plus
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$. For an object $U$, define $\mathcal F^+(U)$ to be the equivalence classes of pairs consisting of a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ and sections $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ whose pullbacks agree after passing to a covering of each $U_i\times_UU_j$, where two pairs are equivalent when they have a common covering refinement on which the sections agree; restrictions are obtained by pullback of coverings and sections. Then $\mathcal F^+$ is separated: for every covering $\{V_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$, the map from $\mathcal F^+(U)$ to the equalizer of the two restriction maps to the pairwise fibre products $V_a\times_UV_b$ is injective. Moreover, the canonical map $\mathcal F^+\to\mathcal F^{++}$ is injective. Equivalently, two plus-construction sections that restrict equally to every member of a covering are equal, and equality of their images in the double plus implies equality in the first plus.

source.place: Sites, Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus), parts (1) and (2), with the plus construction of Section 7.10 and the common-refinement relation used there
